nodes.name: consolidate-logs.sh
nodes.description: Monthly log consolidation and archival script. Compresses logs and reports to tar.gz format and generates monthly index from JSON logs.
responsibilities: Archive guard-dog logs monthly
Compress logs and reports to tar.gz
Generate consolidated monthly index from JSON logs
nodes.error_handling: Silently skips jq errors with 2>/dev/null redirection

nodes.name: git-precommit-hook.sh
nodes.description: Git pre-commit hook that scans package.json changes before commit. Detects new/changed dependencies and runs security scanning via scan-deps.js.
responsibilities: Monitor staged package.json files
Detect new or changed dependencies
Trigger security scan on modified dependencies
Block commits with dangerous packages
outputs: Console output with scan results and decision
installation: Or set globally with: git config --global core.hooksPath ~/guardog/bin/hooks
nodes.decision_logic: Blocks commits (exit 1) if any package.json has dangerous dependencies (BARK decision from scan-deps.js)

nodes.name: mission-control-trigger.js
nodes.description: CLI entry point for Mission Control integration. Accepts single package, file, or batch scanning modes and returns structured JSON for consumption by Mission Control dashboard.
responsibilities: Parse command-line arguments (single package, file, or batch mode)
Load GuardDog analyzer from src/index.js
Execute single or batch package analysis
Format results as structured JSON summary
Return appropriate exit code based on findings
outputs: JSON summary with: timestamp, totalScanned, dangerous, suspicious, safe, packages array
Exit code 0 (all safe) or 1 (dangerous packages found)
nodes.output_format: JSON with threat levels (BARK/WHINE/SILENT) mapped to dangerous/suspicious/safe counts

nodes.name: npm-postinstall-hook.sh
nodes.description: npm postinstall hook that automatically scans packages after npm install. Integrates guard-dog into standard npm workflows for projects.
responsibilities: Detect npm postinstall trigger
Locate project's package.json
Invoke scan-deps.js for dependency scanning
Report results without blocking installation
inputs: INIT_CWD environment variable (set by npm during postinstall)
outputs: Exit code 0 (always, even if scan fails)
nodes.behavior: Non-blocking: scan results are informational only; never prevents npm install from succeeding

nodes.name: setup-logging-structure.sh
nodes.description: One-time initialization script that creates the complete guard-dog and threat-intelligence directory structure, schemas, and configuration templates.
responsibilities: Create guard-dog and threat-intelligence directory trees
Generate logging configuration (.logindex.json files)
Create schema files for installation history, vulnerability tracking, threat data
Generate digest templates for daily reports
Create MANIFEST.md documentation for both agents
Set up archive directories for historical records
outputs: Complete directory structure with subdirectories: logs/, data/, reports/, config/, cache/, feeds/, archive/
Schema JSON files: .logindex.json, install-history/schema.json, vulnerabilities/schema.json, data/schema.json
MANIFEST.md documentation files describing structure and retention policy

nodes.name: threat-intel-daily.js
nodes.description: Daily threat intelligence scanner that collects all workspace packages, queries threat feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA), cross-references findings, and sends Telegram alerts for critical/high issues.
responsibilities: Recursively discover all package.json files in workspace
Collect installed package names and versions
Fetch threat intelligence from multiple feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA, GitHub Advisories)
Query OSV API for version-specific vulnerability lookups
Enrich findings with full summaries from OSV API
Cross-reference threats against installed packages
Separate infrastructure threats (CISA KEV/OS CVEs) from npm/pypi vulnerabilities
Track new findings vs. previous scans to avoid alert fatigue
Send Telegram alerts for critical/high severity findings
Save comprehensive JSON report to data/threat-intel-report.json
inputs: config/config.json for API keys and settings
.env file for Telegram bot token and chat ID
outputs: JSON report at data/threat-intel-report.json with: timestamp, packages scanned, severity breakdown, matches with details, infrastructure threats
Telegram message to configured chat (if configured and findings exist)
Console output with 5-step scan progress and summary
algorithm_steps: 1. Find all package.json files (max depth 5, skip node_modules/.git/dist/build/.next/__pycache__)
2. Collect installed packages with versions from dependencies and devDependencies
3. Fetch threat feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA, GitHub Advisories) for last 7 days
4. Query OSV API for version-specific vulnerabilities in installed packages
5. Enrich findings with full summaries (parallel fetch, concurrency 10)
6. Cross-reference feed findings against installed packages
7. Deduplicate findings and separate npm/pypi from OS/infrastructure CVEs
8. Load previous report to detect new findings and avoid repeat alerts
9. Send Telegram alert if critical/high severity or new findings detected
nodes.threat_separation: npm/pypi vulnerabilities stored in 'matches' array; OS CVEs/CISA KEV threats stored in 'infrastructureThreats' array to prevent confusion with package vulnerabilities
nodes.alert_logic: Sends alert if: critical severity exists, high severity exists, new critical/high finding detected since last scan, or new CISA KEV threat detected

nodes.name: GuardDog class
nodes.description: Main security scanner class that analyzes packages and returns threat decisions with reasoning. Imported by mission-control-trigger.js and threat-intel-daily.js.
responsibilities: Perform single package security analysis
Perform batch package analysis
Return decision (BARK/WHINE/SILENT) with confidence and threat assessment

nodes.name: ThreatIntel class
nodes.description: Threat intelligence aggregator that queries multiple feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA) and performs cross-referencing against installed packages.
responsibilities: Fetch threat data from multiple feeds
Query OSV API for version-specific lookups
Cross-reference threats against installed packages
Separate package vulnerabilities from infrastructure threats
methods: queryPackages(installedPackages) - query OSV for installed packages
crossReference(packages, threats) - match threats to installed packages

nodes.name: TelegramAlert class
nodes.description: Telegram alerting wrapper that formats and sends security findings to a configured Telegram chat.
responsibilities: Format threat findings into readable Telegram messages
Handle bot token and chat ID configuration
Send formatted alerts to Telegram API

nodes.name: scan-deps.js
nodes.description: Dependency scanner utility invoked by git-precommit-hook.sh and npm-postinstall-hook.sh. Scans package.json and compares old vs new versions for changed dependencies.
responsibilities: Parse package.json file
Compare old and new package versions (when --changed-only flag used)
Invoke GuardDog analysis on dependencies
Return scan results and appropriate exit code

nodes.name: module-loader.js
nodes.description: ESM module loader utility that enables dynamic imports from absolute file paths. Used by mission-control-trigger.js and threat-intel-daily.js.
responsibilities: Load ESM modules from absolute paths
Handle dynamic imports for guard-dog classes

execution_flows.name: Pre-Commit Security Check
steps: Git executes pre-commit hook: git-precommit-hook.sh
Hook checks for staged package.json files
If package.json changed: invoke scan-deps.js with old vs new comparison
scan-deps.js uses GuardDog to analyze changed dependencies
GuardDog returns decision (BARK/WHINE/SILENT) for each package
Hook blocks commit (exit 1) if any package decision is BARK (dangerous)
Hook allows commit (exit 0) if all packages are WHINE or SILENT
execution_flows.outcome: Commit is blocked or allowed based on dependency security assessment

execution_flows.name: Post-Install Security Scan
steps: npm postinstall phase executes npm-postinstall-hook.sh
Hook locates project's package.json
Hook invokes scan-deps.js to scan all dependencies
scan-deps.js uses GuardDog to analyze all packages
GuardDog returns decision for each dependency
Results logged to console (informational only)
npm install succeeds regardless of scan outcome
execution_flows.outcome: Dependencies are scanned and logged; installation is never blocked

execution_flows.name: On-Demand Package Scan (Mission Control)
steps: Mission Control invokes: mission-control-trigger.js <package> [ecosystem]
Trigger script loads GuardDog class via module-loader
GuardDog.analyze() returns single package assessment
Trigger script formats results as JSON summary
JSON includes: timestamp, threat level (BARK/WHINE/SILENT), confidence, reasons
Results output to stdout for Mission Control to consume
Exit code indicates overall safety (0=safe or mixed, 1=dangerous)
execution_flows.outcome: Mission Control receives JSON-formatted security assessment

execution_flows.name: Batch Package Scan (Mission Control)
steps: Mission Control invokes: mission-control-trigger.js --batch packages.json
Trigger script loads JSON array of packages
GuardDog.batchAnalyze() analyzes all packages in parallel
Each package receives BARK/WHINE/SILENT decision
Trigger script aggregates results: count dangerous, suspicious, safe
JSON summary output includes all package details with decisions
Exit code indicates if any package is dangerous (exit 1)
execution_flows.outcome: Mission Control receives aggregated batch assessment

execution_flows.name: Daily Threat Intelligence Scan
steps: threat-intel-daily.js executes
Recursively find all package.json files in workspace (depth 5, skip build dirs)
Collect installed package names and versions
ThreatIntel.fetchAll() queries threat feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA, GitHub Advisories) for last 7 days
ThreatIntel.queryPackages() queries OSV API for version-specific vulns of installed packages
Enrich OSV findings in parallel (max 10 concurrent) to get full summaries
ThreatIntel.crossReference() matches threats against installed packages
Deduplicates findings and separates npm/pypi vulnerabilities from OS/infrastructure CVEs
Load previous report and identify new findings (avoid alert fatigue)
Build comprehensive JSON report with severity breakdown
Write report to data/threat-intel-report.json
Evaluate alert criteria: critical/high severity exists, or new critical/high/CISA threats found
If alert criteria met: TelegramAlert.send() formats and posts message to Telegram
Log summary to console with 5-step progress and statistics
execution_flows.outcome: Comprehensive threat report generated; Telegram alert sent if critical/high findings detected

execution_flows.name: Monthly Log Consolidation
steps: consolidate-logs.sh executes
Create archive directory: archive/YYYY/MM/
Compress all logs and reports to tar.gz: logs-YYYY-MM.tar.gz
Use jq to consolidate all JSON logs into single month-index.json
Write consolidated index to archive/YYYY/MM/month-index.json
Log success message with archive path
execution_flows.outcome: Monthly log archive created; consolidated index generated for historical analysis
